hook_text: A quarter of a metre of lace. Is that 4 cm or 25 cm? The sewing shop needs to know.
clip_script: Sewing shop in Upington. A quarter of a metre of lace. A metre is 100 centimetres. A quarter is 100 split into 4: 25 centimetres, not 4. Half a metre? 50. Three quarters? 75. Now a builder: 2 metre plank, cut off 45 centimetres. Change to centimetres: 200 minus 45 is 155 centimetres, 1 metre 55. And the school track: 400 metres a lap, 5 laps, 2 000 metres, 2 kilometres. Watch the zeros: 1 metre 5 centimetres is 105, not 150. 10, 100, 1 000, and always write the unit.
visual_style: Whiteboard metre stick split into quarters at 25, 50 and 75; a plank being sawn; a running track with lap counters.
pacing: The lace puzzle, quarters of a metre, the plank, the track, then the zero trap.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and work out how many 25 cm pieces you can cut from 2 metres of string.
